create.name: Missouri Zen Center
create.bio:
Missouri Zen Center is a small Soto Zen temple in a white clapboard house in Webster Groves, a suburb of St. Louis. Its founder and abbot, Rosan Osamu Yoshida, came to Zen through a university meditation group in Tokyo, sat with teachers in New York and Nebraska, and was ordained and later given Dharma transmission by Dainin Katagiri; he also trained at Zuioji in Japan and taught comparative religion at Toyo University. The centre began in 1979 and became a non-profit the following year, and it has offered zazen in the St. Louis area ever since.

The sangha meets for regular zazen and chanting, and holds weekend sesshins with formal oryoki meals, work practice and a Dharma talk. A Monday Beginner's Night introduces Buddhism and sitting meditation, followed by a period of zazen and questions with the abbot. The temple keeps a lending library of more than a thousand Buddhist books, and its teaching rests on three themes the founder champions: the awakened way, a global ethic shared across religions, and voluntary simplicity. Translations, a zazen manual and a bilingual blog of talks are free on its website.

courses.title: Beginner's Night
courses.description: A Monday evening class for newcomers and students of religion: a short introduction to Buddhism and sitting from a student teacher, twenty minutes of zazen with the abbot, then his explanation of Zen and time for questions. Attendees are asked to register by email two days ahead.

courses.title: Sesshins
courses.description: Weekend retreats running from Friday evening to Sunday, with many periods of zazen broken by walking meditation, formal oryoki meals with chanting, work practice, a Dharma talk and at times a private interview with the teacher, all held in silence. Dates are posted on the centre's calendar.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Members support the house, grounds and daily sitting schedule, and may borrow from the centre's library of Buddhist books and videos; membership also sustains the abbot's classes and the monthly retreats.

free_resources.title: Mechanics of Zazen & Kinhin
free_resources.description: Step-by-step guidance on entering the zendo, sitting posture, eyes and breathing, working with thoughts and the form of slow walking meditation, introduced by a passage from Dogen's Fukanzazengi.

free_resources.title: Document Downloads
free_resources.description: Free PDFs from the centre, including the abbot's translation of Dogen's Fukanzazengi, a manual of zazen, the Sunday service text and a welcome leaflet.

free_resources.title: MZC Here-Now
free_resources.description: The centre's blog of short Dharma reflections drawn from talks at the temple, many in both English and Japanese, linking Buddhist teaching with daily life and care for the natural world.
